ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, containing a left/lower carbon skeleton, an upper HN group connected to a short alkyl line, a central carbon connected to OH on the right, and CHO labeled at the bottom. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: Count the bonds between non-hydrogen atoms from top to bottom and from left to right, excluding N-H, O-H, and C-H. The countable non-hydrogen bonds are: 1 bond from N to the upper alkyl/methyl group, 1 bond from N to the central/ring carbon, 1 bond from the central carbon to the left carbon skeleton, 1 bond from the central carbon to the O in OH, 2 C-C bonds in the left/lower carbon skeleton, and 1 C-O bond in the CHO group. The total is 1+1+1+1+2+1=7.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Scan the image from top to bottom and left to right. Count each visible straight bond between two non-H atoms: the N-to-methyl/alkyl bond at the top, the N-to-ring/central carbon bond, the central carbon-to-left carbon skeleton bond, the central carbon-to-O bond of OH, the two C-C bonds along the left/bottom carbon skeleton, and the C-to-O bond in the CHO group. Exclude N-H, O-H, C-H bonds and ignore all curved arrows. Sum these non-hydrogen bonds to obtain 7.

method.method_draft: Convert the transition-state structure into a heavy-atom graph. Assign nodes for the N, its carbon substituent, the central carbon, the OH oxygen, the adjacent carbon skeleton vertices, the aldehyde carbon, and the aldehyde oxygen. Enumerate unique heavy-atom adjacencies visible in the drawing: N-C substituent, N-central C, central C-skeleton C, central C-OH O, skeleton C-skeleton C, skeleton C-aldehyde C, and aldehyde C-O. Do not add edges for H in HN, OH, or CHO. Counting these unique graph edges gives 7.
